_note:
Slots for [brg_home-hero]. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {token} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. Slot names are underscore-only. `text`/`textarea`/`lines` defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters — a literal `&` and a literal `—`, never `&` or `—`.\n\nTHE

IS NOW WIRED, as type `lines`. It was declined on 2026-08-13 for one reason only: the headline carries a structural break — `We're in the business / of making your day great.` — and no slot type could carry it. text/textarea escaped it into a visible <br> and html returned

-wrapped content nested inside the

. `lines` escapes first and turns the editor's newline into
after, which expresses the break without the field accepting markup. The constraint was real; it stopped being a constraint when the type existed.

cta_label.label: Button label
cta_label.doc: The wording on the hero button. Short reads best — it sits under the tagline.

cta_href.label: Button link
cta_href.doc: Where the hero button goes. A path like /brands/ stays on this site; a full address goes off it.

heading.label: Headline
heading.doc: The hero headline. PRESS RETURN where you want the line to break — it breaks exactly there. Two lines is the design; three starts eating the fold on a phone.
heading.default:
We're in the business
of making your day great.

sub.label: Sub copy
sub.doc: Sits under the marker underline, capped at 52ch. Plain text; markup is escaped. Write `&` and `—` as literal characters. PRESS RETURN to force a line break exactly where you want one.
sub.default: From a classic Board & Brew sandwich to a slice at Odie's — we're here for the moments that matter.

tagline.label: Yellow tagline
tagline.doc: The short line beneath the sub, in the display face. White, not yellow, per the comp. ~40 characters.
tagline.default: Good food. Real people. Rad experience.

uline_variant.label: Underline animation
uline_variant.doc: How the hand-drawn underline reveals. `u3` (default) filled brush + ~5deg angled wipe — keeps the taper. `wipe` straight-edged reveal, the conservative fallback with no skewed edge to overhang. `u1` scaleX bar, the lab's baseline, kept so the taper argument can be re-checked live. Unknown or blank renders the mark STATIC and visible, never hidden. u2/u4 (dasharray draws) need the artwork inline as SVG and are not available on an . Catalog: website/lab/README.md.

bg_photo.label: Background photo
bg_photo.doc: The full-bleed hero collage behind the logo and headline. Dark imagery works best — the headline and sub copy sit on top in white. Landscape, at least 1600px wide. Leave empty to keep the current picture.

bg_photo_mobile.label: Background photo — phones
bg_photo_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the hero photo for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave empty and the main photo above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main photo is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or tighter version reads far better.

photo_strength.label: Background photo — strength
photo_strength.doc: How strongly the background collage shows, as a percentage. THIS IS USUALLY THE ONE YOU WANT. The hero has always held this photo at 42%, which is most of why it reads as dark; the two vignette settings below only darken what is left. Raise this toward 100 to bring the picture forward. The white headline needs some darkness behind it, so check the headline is still easy to read after a big change.

veil_center.label: Vignette — middle
veil_center.doc: How dark the middle of the hero is, behind the headline, as a percentage. 58 is the value this hero has always used. Lower lets more of the photo through in the middle; higher pushes the picture further back.

veil_edge.label: Vignette — edges
veil_edge.doc: How dark the outer edges are, as a percentage. 90 is the value this hero has always used. This is the setting that makes the corners almost black. The darkness fades smoothly between this and the middle value above.

bg_photo_tone.label: Background photo — color
bg_photo_tone.doc: Color is the default. Switch this photo to black and white when you want it that way on purpose — the photography on this site was only ever gray because the placeholder images were. Affects this photo alone.

bg_photo_px.label: Background photo — movement
bg_photo_px.doc: How far this photo drifts inside its frame as you scroll, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The dropdown this replaces offered 6, 10 and 16 as Subtle, Medium and Strong, so anything already set still reads exactly the same — you can now pick the values in between. 40 is the ceiling: the page itself stops there, so a larger number would do nothing. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed.

bg_photo_px_dir.label: Background photo — movement direction
bg_photo_px_dir.doc: Which way this photo travels as the page scrolls. Neighboring photos set in opposite directions are what reads as depth.

video_id.label: Background video (optional)
video_id.doc: Paste a YouTube or Vimeo link, or just the ID. Leave blank and the photo above is used. The video plays silently on a loop with no controls, and the photo shows while it loads, if the video is blocked, or for visitors who have switched off animation.

video_source.label: Video from
video_source.doc: Which service the link is from. Only matters when a video is set.

overlay_color.label: Overlay color
overlay_color.doc: A flat color laid over the background photo to keep the headline readable. This does nothing when no photo is set. Choose None to turn the overlay off entirely.

overlay_strength.label: Overlay strength
overlay_strength.doc: How much of the overlay color shows through. Only has an effect once an overlay color is chosen above. 45% is the usual setting for white type over a photo — go higher if the headline still fights the picture, lower if the photo is already dark.

section_bg.label: Section background
section_bg.doc: A pattern or photo filling this whole section, behind everything else. Leave it empty — as it is now — and the section keeps the plain color it has today; nothing changes until you choose something. It is cropped to fill, so the exact size does not matter. ON A DARK SECTION USE A LIGHT OR GRAY ARTWORK: a black pattern over a black panel stays invisible however high you set the strength below. ON THE HOME HERO IT IS EFFECTIVELY HIDDEN: the collage is always present and a vignette sits over it, so this layer is behind both. It is here for consistency, not because it will show.

section_bg_opacity.label: Background strength
section_bg_opacity.doc: How strongly the background shows through. Choose 100% when the artwork already has the intended strength built into the file — anything lower then fades a graphic that was supplied ready to use. Use the lower values when a full-strength image would compete with the words in front of it.

section_bg_px.label: Background movement
section_bg_px.doc: Drifts the background as the page scrolls, behind the content, as a percentage of the section's height. 0 is off — the right starting point, because a pattern moving too fast pulls the eye away from the copy. 6 is subtle, 10 medium, 16 strong, and anything in between is allowed. 40 is the ceiling; the page stops there.

section_bg_px_dir.label: Background movement direction
section_bg_px_dir.doc: Which way the background travels as the page scrolls. Only matters once movement above is above 0. Neighboring sections set in opposite directions are what reads as depth rather than as one sheet sliding.

section_bg_mobile.label: Section background — phones
section_bg_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the background for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave it empty and the main background above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main artwork is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or simplified version reads far better.

mark_1_smile_art.label: Artwork
mark_1_smile_art.doc: Which mark is drawn here. Leave it alone to keep the one the design uses. Any SVG or PNG from the media library works; SVG stays crisp at any size.

mark_1_smile_pos.label: Position
mark_1_smile_pos.doc: Where the mark sits in its section. "Where the design put it" is the starting point and leaves it exactly where it is now — choose one of the nine only when you want to move it. Corners sit inside the section padding, so a long headline cannot push a mark down into the type.

mark_1_smile_opacity.label: Opacity
mark_1_smile_opacity.doc: How solid the mark is. 100 is as drawn; lower settles it into the background.

mark_1_smile_show.label: Show this mark
mark_1_smile_show.doc: Hiding removes just this one mark. Nothing else in the section changes.

mark_1_smile_anim.label: Animation
mark_1_smile_anim.doc: How the mark moves. "As built" keeps what it does today — a hard-cut jitter for most, a spin for the asterisk in the hero cluster. Still stops it entirely. Anyone who has switched off animation in their system settings sees it still whatever is chosen here.

btn_color.label: Button color
btn_color.doc: The button's color. "As designed" is the starting point and leaves this section's buttons exactly as they look today — which matters, because several sections paint theirs black on purpose and the give-back slider alternates yellow and black down the slides. Choose a color and it takes over. The words flip to black or white automatically, whichever reads on the color you pick. This applies to every button in this section.

btn_style.label: Filled or outline
btn_style.doc: Filled is a solid block of color. Outline draws the color as a ring with the words in it and nothing behind — useful over a photo, where a solid block can sit heavily. "As designed" leaves it as it is today, which is filled everywhere. Both are exactly the same size, so switching one does not move anything around it.

btn_effect.label: Hover effect
btn_effect.doc:
What the button does when someone points at it. Lift is what every button has always done and stays the default — it rises slightly and casts a shadow. Lift and swap color does that AND flips to the opposite ink, which is the loudest of the set and best kept for one main action on a page. Underline draws a rule under the words and leaves the button still, which reads as a link — a good fit for the small buttons. Grow swells it in place. Press down pushes it into the page. Fill in floods an outline button with its color, so pair it with Outline. None holds it still.

This is the HOVER only; the way the button arrives on screen is the site-wide reveal. Anyone who has switched off animation sees no hover movement whatever is chosen.

buttons.label: Buttons
buttons.doc:
Buttons for this section. Add as many as you need — they sit in a row and wrap onto the next line on a narrow screen. Leave the list empty, as it is now, and the section has no buttons at all and looks exactly as it does today.

Their color, fill and hover come from Button style below and apply to all of them.

label.label: Label
label.doc: The words on the button. Short reads best: it is set in capitals with wide letter spacing. A button with no label is not drawn.

href.label: Link
href.doc: Where it goes. A path like /careers/ stays on this site, a full address goes off it, and mailto:someone@blacktoprg.com opens a mail window.

popup.label: Open in a pop-up
popup.doc: For a Google Form, choose Pop-up and it opens in a panel over the page instead of sending people to Google. A form that is set to require a Google sign-in CANNOT be shown this way — Google's sign-in page refuses to be embedded and the panel comes up blank — so that one has to stay on Open the link until its Responses settings are changed. Anything that is not a form stays on Open the link.

cta_position.label: Where the buttons sit
cta_position.doc: At the bottom is the usual place and the one the rest of the site uses. This section has no heading, so the bottom is the only position offered.

choices.foot: At the bottom of the section

modal_bg.label: Pop-up background
modal_bg.doc: The color of the panel a form opens in. Match it to the form's own Theme color in Google Forms and the two read as one surface. This cannot color the form itself — that is Google's page on Google's domain.
